# Run and drive a run from a program

<!-- description: The functions a program calls to step, advance, answer and abandon runs, with the option and reply types they use. -->

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-library-reference.mjs from the API reports and the built declarations; do not edit by hand: after `npm run build`, run `npm run docs:library`. -->

A program that drives runs itself calls these functions with a `RunStore` and a `WorkflowDefinition`: `executeStep`, `executeChain` and `advanceRun` move a run forward, `submitHumanResponse` answers an open question, and `abandonRun` ends a run. Each returns an `EngineReply`, except `abandonRun`, which returns the run's `RunRecord`. This page lists them, the other functions the docs name for driving runs, and every type they reach that no more specific page holds.

Where the docs teach it: [Core library: run a workflow from your own program](../core-library.md#run-a-workflow-from-your-own-program).

## Functions

### abandonRun

function · public

Explicitly abandon a run by stamping the authoritative `abandoned_at` marker. The run's phase
derives to `abandoned` (via `deriveRunPhase`) regardless of `failed_steps`/`terminal_reason`.

Behavior:
- Missing run → propagates `STATE_RUN_NOT_FOUND` (from `store.get`).
- Already abandoned (`abandoned_at` set) → idempotent no-op, returns the existing run.
- A LIVE gate (`pending_gate` set) → throws `STATE_TRANSITION_DENIED` carrying
  `gate_id`/`step_name`/`choices` in `details`; each surface names its own answer verb. Keyed on
  the gate, never the persisted label: a #432-class record (label `gate_waiting`, no
  `pending_gate`) has nothing to answer and abandons like the `running` run it derives to.
- Terminal (`completed`/`failed`/`aborted`) → throws `STATE_RUN_TERMINAL` (do not clobber a finished run).
- Otherwise (`running`) → stamps `abandoned_at`, sets `terminal_state:true` + `terminal_reason`.
- Releases every claim in the same write (`in_progress_steps: []`, `claims: {}`) — the shape
  `applyResume` already performs unconditionally. A terminal run cannot progress:
  `claimStep` finds no eligible step (`findEligibleSteps` returns `[]` for `terminal_state`) and
  refuses `STATE_STEP_NOT_ELIGIBLE`; `reclaimStep` and `append_trace` refuse terminal by name.
  So a kept claim only ever blocked `purge`. The brake on purging a just-abandoned run is
  `--older-than`, never a fossil claim.

Concurrency: if `update()` raises `STATE_SNAPSHOT_MISMATCH`, the run is reloaded once — if it is now
abandoned, that is idempotent success; otherwise the mismatch is propagated (the run changed under
us — likely a live runner — and abandon should lose). No retry loop beyond the single reload.

```ts
function abandonRun(store: RunStore, runId: string, reason?: string, actor?: {
    by: Attributed;
    door?: 'realm_run_abandon' | 'abandon_run';
}): Promise<RunRecord>;
```

### advanceRun

function · public

Runs what the engine owes on a run, its eligible guards and then its eligible `auto` steps, from
the stored record. The reply carries, privately, the snapshot it was judged on
(`judgedSnapshotOf`).
Its contract is the body's, documented below.

```ts
function advanceRun(store: RunStore, definition: WorkflowDefinition, options: AdvanceRunOptions): Promise<EngineReply>;
```

### buildDisclosureSet

function · public

The one builder of a disclosure set: every surface builds its set here.
Every
surface builds its set here: the environment's members through `environmentEntries` (or
none, with `environment: 'not_swept'` and cause `host_set`, when the caller passes no
environment), the declared values by name, then `compileDisclosure`.

```ts
function buildDisclosureSet(input: {
    env: Readonly<Record<string, string | undefined>> | undefined;
    declared: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
    declaredState: DeclaredState;
    declaredCause?: DeclaredCause;
    audience: DisclosureAudience;
    notSecret?: readonly string[];
    cwd?: string;
}): {
    set: DisclosureSet;
    unmaskable: string[];
};
```

### callsHostDispatcher

function · public

Whether Realm calls the host's dispatcher for a step: yes unless the step is missing, a guard, a
finalizer, or an `auto` step with a handler or a service. The engine settles guards and
finalizers itself, and an `auto` step with a handler or a service runs that handler or adapter.
So: every `agent` step, every bare
`auto` step, and a step whose `execution` is missing or unknown. The one predicate admission's
`required_parts` row and `makeCall`'s dispatcher branch both serve. A step that is not an object
(`null`, a string, … — a definition the host built wrong) is not one: no error escapes here.

```ts
function callsHostDispatcher(step: StepDefinition | undefined): boolean;
```

### claimStepForDrive

function · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

Takes step `stepName`'s claim for this program, under a lease it holds, before the step's work
starts.
In order: the store keeps no leases ⇒ `unleased_store`
(nothing held, read or written); the store's `leases.hold()` cannot make one ⇒ `lease_unavailable`;
the run is loaded and the step judged by `admitWay('run_step')` as this program; then the store's
`claimStep` writes the claim under the hold ⇒ `claimed`. When the store refuses the claim
(`STATE_STEP_ALREADY_CLAIMED`, `STATE_STEP_NOT_ELIGIBLE`), a fresh read is judged again — the step
may have settled meanwhile — or the loaded run when that read throws. Every answer but `claimed`
closes the hold with the record it was judged on. Any other error is thrown unchanged, after the
hold is closed: with no record when `claimStep` threw it (the write may have landed), else with the
newest record the call holds, or none.

```ts
function claimStepForDrive(store: RunStore, runId: string, stepName: string, options: ClaimStepForDriveOptions): Promise<DriveClaim>;
```

### classifyRunHealth

function · public

Classifies a run's health into zero or more typed findings. Pure, read-only, definition-
optional, judged at the snapshot's `at` (#715 (b)). See the module doc above for the full branch-conditioning table
(design record §1, fold B1) and the honest-admission rule.

```ts
function classifyRunHealth(snapshot: ListedSnapshot, opts?: ClassifyRunHealthOptions): RunHealthFinding[];
```

### classifyStop

function · public

What kind of stop a loop met on a step it picked or ran, from the reply and the record read again
after it. It is asked only by a loop (core's advance loop, `realm run advance`, `realm agent`,
`realm workflow run`), never of a direct `execute_step` call's own reply, which is the reply.
First matching row wins:

1. `blocked`, `STATE_STEP_ALREADY_CLAIMED` → `held_elsewhere`.
2. `blocked` with no code, about `step` (not eligible on the engine's own read, or a failed
   precondition): the step in flight, completed or failed → `held_elsewhere`; else the run ended →
   `run_ended`; else a question is open → `question_open`; else none (a precondition block —
   hosts render it as before).
3. `error`, `STATE_STEP_ALREADY_SETTLED`, `STATE_CLAIM_LOST` or `STATE_RUN_TERMINAL`, about `step`
   (`ran_here`): the run not ended and the step in progress → `held_elsewhere`; else the step
   settled → `step_settled`; else the run ended → `run_ended`; else → `claim_removed`.
4. `error`, `STATE_STEP_NOT_ELIGIBLE`, about `step` (the claim's re-check): the run ended →
   `run_ended`; else a question is open → `question_open`; else → `not_eligible`.
5. `error`, `ENGINE_HANDLER_NOT_REGISTERED` or `ENGINE_ADAPTER_NOT_REGISTERED` →
   `capability_missing`.
6. Any other `error`: the record lists the step it is about (`stopAbout`) as failed →
   `failed`; else → `refused`.

`undefined` for any other reply (`ok`, `confirm_required`, a `blocked` reply rows 1–2 do not take).

```ts
function classifyStop(reply: StopReply, step: string | undefined, record: StopRecord): StopClassification | undefined;
```

### damagedFileConcerns

function · public

Whether a damaged run file can concern a workflow: the one scope test of the keyed fallback scan
and of every workflow-scoped read.
False when the file is JSON that is
not an object (it names no workflow and holds no key), when it is a folder named like a run file
(`unreadable` with `EISDIR`: it holds no run and no key, F6.3), and when its object names ANOTHER
workflow by a string `workflow_id`; true otherwise — a file whose content cannot be read
(`unreadable`, `empty`, not JSON), an object with no string `workflow_id`, or one naming this
workflow.

```ts
function damagedFileConcerns(reading: {
    facts: UnreadableFileFacts;
    object?: Record<string, unknown>;
}, workflowId: string): boolean;
```

### deriveRunPhase

function · public

Derives the `run_phase` from the run record's fields. Called after every store write to keep
run_phase consistent — this function's return value is ALWAYS what gets persisted (issue #279,
increment 2, PR-C — the PHASE_IS_GENERATED law): callers must never persist a raw/stale
`run_phase` value, and every reader that needs the true phase should prefer this derivation over
a possibly-stale persisted field (design record `design-d5-increment2.md` §5 D-3's disposal
rule: "control flow keys on `terminal_state`, the terminal marker fields, or DERIVED phase —
never on persisted `run_phase`; persisted `run_phase` is render-only, and rendered only after
derivation").

Issue #279 (increment 2, PR-C — the #282 class closure, D-3 leg i): the WHOLE terminal cluster
(abandoned_at → aborted_at → terminal_state's own completed/failed/abandoned split) is now
checked ABOVE `pending_gate` — reordered from a prior shape that checked `pending_gate` SECOND,
right after `abandoned_at`, before `terminal_state` was ever consulted. That prior order let a
TERMINAL run that still carries a leftover/grandfathered `pending_gate` (the #282 class: any
write path that terminalizes a run without also clearing `pending_gate` — a legacy/pre-#279
writer, or a mixed-fleet reintroduction) derive as `'gate_waiting'` forever, even though the run
had already reached a real terminal outcome. The fix is a pure reordering — every non-#282
record (a genuinely non-terminal run with a live open gate, or a terminal run that legitimately
never had a gate) derives IDENTICALLY either way; only the one previously-mis-derived class
changes, and it changes to the CORRECT phase.

```ts
function deriveRunPhase(run: Pick<RunRecord, 'pending_gate' | 'terminal_state' | 'failed_steps' | 'terminal_reason' | 'aborted_at' | 'abandoned_at' | 'sealed_by'>): RunPhase;
```

### describePending

function · public

What the run owes, from the record, the definition and (when present) the registry, at the
snapshot's `at`. Pure. A terminal run owes nothing; so does a run with an open gate — except a
question whose time is up at `at` and that declares `on_expiry` (decision C95): carrying it out is
owed engine work (`expiry_due`, the `advance_run` act), and the question can no longer be answered.
#715 (b) (D6-17): it judges ONE snapshot — the record with the reading it was read or written at —
so the view and the record can never be judged at two instants; no caller reads a clock for it.
An eligible agent step is judged by the checks that read no input
(`AGENT_PRE_CLAIM_REFUSALS`, decision C82): one the run refuses is listed in
`agent_refused`, never in `agent_steps` or `agent_actions`.

```ts
function describePending(definition: WorkflowDefinition, snapshot: Snapshot, registry: ExtensionRegistry | undefined): PendingView;
```

### describeStoredFileFault

function · public

The words for what is wrong with a stored file, as a clause after its subject, with no parser
text and no position.
A registered copy keeps its shipped nouns ("not a workflow object", "empty
(0 bytes) — not a workflow").

```ts
function describeStoredFileFault(facts: UnreadableFileFacts): string;
```

### disclose

function · public

Hides every member of `set` and, with `tier: 'all'`, every pattern, in `text`. Everything is
marked on the ORIGINAL text, then each maximal marked run is written as ONE `REDACTED_MARKER`:
a short member inside a longer one leaves no fragment, and two side by side become one marker. It
never matches inside a named marker (I11), so disclosing twice changes nothing.

- members: every form of every member; with `tier: 'declared'` only the declared ones (question
  text, a private terminal);
- patterns (`tier: 'all'`): `Bearer `, `Basic ` and `token=` runs; a URL's user part; and the
  value after any credential name (`<name>=`, `<name>:`, `"<name>": "…"`) — inside JSON to the first
  unescaped quote, otherwise to whitespace, `&`, `;` or `,`. For `authorization`, the
  scheme word and the credential after it are both hidden.

`hidden` counts the runs by the highest kind inside each; `unchecked` is 0 (PR-M1 fills it).

```ts
function disclose(text: string, set: DisclosureSet, tier: DisclosureTier): Disclosed;
```

### discloseLeaf

function · public

The disclosure walk's leaf transform for one string at `tier`: `discloseText`, then the
escaped-spelling check, exactly as the walk applies them to a `value` leaf.
It IS the walk's
leaf (`walkValue` calls the same two functions on a string; a cell checks equality over the disclosure-law corpus),
exported so the MCP door can tell when the walk would transform a prompt beyond `disclose` — on
such a prompt the door publishes no `stable_prefix`.

```ts
function discloseLeaf(text: string, set: DisclosureSet, tier: DisclosureTier): string;
```

### discloseSplit

function · public

`disclose` cut in two at `cut`, from the one marking pass `disclose` uses. `cut` is in input
coordinates, clamped to `[0, text.length]`.
A marked run
that crosses the cut (`marks[cut-1] ≠ 0 ∧ marks[cut] ≠ 0`) moves the cut back to the run's start —
across two adjacent runs, to the first one's start, since adjacent marks are one run — so no head
ever holds part of a hidden value, and `head + tail` is exactly `disclose`'s text (the law cell
proves it at every cut). Callers (pinned by a source cell): `discloseForAgentSplit` (the CLI), the
MCP door's `stable_prefix`, and `discloseSplitSize`. Never a print path or the writer.

```ts
function discloseSplit(text: string, cut: number, set: DisclosureSet, tier: DisclosureTier): DisclosedSplit;
```

### discloseSplitSize

function · public

The sizes of `discloseSplit`'s pieces and nothing of their text, for a caller that must never
hold a disclosed head. Numbers only: the describer of `validate`, `register` and `watch` imports
this, never `discloseSplit`.
`headAsciiChars` counts the
head's UTF-16 code units below 0x80, so the describer's token interval is the one its text gives.

```ts
function discloseSplitSize(text: string, cut: number, set: DisclosureSet, tier: DisclosureTier): DisclosedSplitSize;
```

### displayId

function · public

An id a file holds, as text may show it: as it is when made of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`
and at most 64 characters, else `another run id (not shown)`. A file's content can hold anything,
a newline or a terminal escape included.

```ts
function displayId(id: string): string;
```

### drainFinalizers

function · public

Drains a run's pending finalizers, the lowest-ranked first, re-reading the record after every
settle, lease or mark.
Drains the
LOWEST-ranked pending finalizer, re-reading the record returned by the LAST settle/lease/mark at
every step — NEVER a pass-start snapshot (the DRAIN_REREADS_LEDGER pin: a snapshot taken once at
the top of this function would go stale the instant the first lease/mark commits, silently
reintroducing exactly the kind of pre-commit assumption #279 exists to eliminate).

Lives here (not in settlement.ts) so the module-private `withTimeout`/`callHandler` — shared
with the step dispatch above — are reused without exporting them; `settlement.ts` stays
pure/no-I/O (design record §7 CS-purity).

Registry pre-check: an absent handler leaves the entry pending and discloses why, rather than
burning it (leasing it, failing the call, and marking it 'failed' would destroy the "recoverable
on a capable runner" property a still-pending entry carries). Rank-monotonic: a pass HALTS at the
first entry it cannot lease/execute, so a lower-ranked absent-handler or held-lease entry
withholds every higher-ranked (later) finalizer behind it (R11) — this is deliberate: rank order
is a DELIVERY order guarantee, not just a preference.

`not_eligible` at lease OR mark time is a contract violation (an unknown finalizer id — mintFresh
only ever mints real workflow finalizer names) and aborts the pass LOUD (throws), distinct from
`ledger_not_pending` at lease time, which ADVANCES (someone else already resolved it). A
non-BUSY infra throw from `mark_finalizer` also aborts loud, with the remaining-pending list in
the message. The executed-but-not-recorded warning (three reasons: `lease_lost`,
`ledger_not_pending`-AFTER-execution, `run_not_terminal`) halts the pass rather than continuing —
each of those three reasons refuses the mark WITHOUT mutating the ledger entry's `'pending'`
status, so continuing would re-select the SAME entry next iteration (an infinite loop); halting
is the only forward-progress-safe response until an operator or a later terminal edge resolves it.

```ts
function drainFinalizers(store: RunStore, definition: WorkflowDefinition, registry: ExtensionRegistry | undefined, runId: string, driver?: Attributed): Promise<{
    run: RunRecord;
    at: Date;
    snapshot: Snapshot;
    warnings: string[];
    leftPending: string[];
    attempted: string[];
}>;
```

### executeChain

function · public

Runs the step `options.command` names, then the `auto` steps after it, stopping at an agent step,
a gate, an error or the run's end. The reply carries, privately, the snapshot it was judged on
(`judgedSnapshotOf`).
Its contract is the body's, documented below.

```ts
function executeChain(store: RunStore, definition: WorkflowDefinition, options: ExecuteChainOptions): Promise<EngineReply>;
```

### executeEngineStep

function · public

The one way the engine runs an `auto` step it owns: `executeStep` with the engine's own input.
For a bare step it applies the core bare-step rule.
The advance loop runs every step it picks through this; `realm agent`'s exit for
an engine step that cannot run here (decision C23) makes its one attempt through it too, so no
host composes an engine step's input itself.

It runs ONLY steps whose `execution` is `'auto'` (decision C83). A step of any other kind — an
agent step (a driver answers it), a guard (settled by the advance loop and the settlement
cascade), a finalizer (run by the drain) — is refused before anything is read or written: the
function throws a `WorkflowError` (`ENGINE_INTERNAL`, `agentAction: 'stop'`) whose message names
the step and its kind, and the run record is unchanged. A host that names such a step has a
wiring defect, the same on every call, so it throws like the admission rule's host tier. A step
the definition does not have is left to `executeStep`'s own refusal.

```ts
function executeEngineStep(store: RunStore, definition: WorkflowDefinition, options: ExecuteEngineStepOptions): Promise<EngineReply>;
```

### executeStep

function · public

Runs the one step `options.command` names with the caller's input and returns the engine's reply;
unlike `executeChain`, it does not go on to the `auto` steps after it.

```ts
function executeStep(store: RunStore, definition: WorkflowDefinition, options: ExecuteStepOptions): Promise<EngineReply>;
```

### findEligibleSteps

function · public

Returns the names of all steps currently eligible for execution.
Gate serialization: if any gate is open, no steps are eligible.
A step is eligible if:
  - not already completed, in-progress, failed, or skipped
  - trigger_rule is satisfied
  - when-condition (if present) is truthy

```ts
function findEligibleSteps(definition: WorkflowDefinition, run: ListedRecord): string[];
```

### getWorkflowForRun

function · public

Fetches the workflow definition a run needs, turning a `STATE_WORKFLOW_NOT_FOUND` into an error
that says how to register it. It is the one place every run-context site calls (`respond`,
`resume`, `replay`, `drain`, `agent --run-id`, and the MCP
`submit_human_response`/`execute_step`/`append_trace` tools), instead of each wrapping its own
raw `store.get(run.workflow_id)`.

The `store` and `run` parameters are narrowed to exactly what this function uses
(`Pick<WorkflowRegistrar, 'get'>` / `Pick<RunRecord, 'workflow_id'>`) — by necessity, not taste:
`resolveRunAttach`'s own dependency type IS that narrower `Pick` (its test doubles are get-only,
and a full `WorkflowRegistrar` parameter here would not compile at that call site). Every other
caller passes a full registrar and a full run record, both structurally assignable to the
narrower type.

HEDGED reasoning, moved here from `run-attach.ts`'s inline comment (its call site now just
points back here): this function genuinely cannot know WHY the workflow is missing. A wiped
store, a different `$HOME`, and a run created from a file without `--register` all mint the
identical `STATE_WORKFLOW_NOT_FOUND` from the registrar — so the remedy says "most often",
never "because". Keyed on the stable error CODE, never on message text.

PRECONDITION — run-context resolution ONLY. A by-id lookup with no run behind it (`start_run`,
`start_run_batch`, `get_workflow_protocol`) must never call this: there the hedge would be
false — "this run was created from a file without --register" presumes a run that does not
exist yet.

Every OTHER `WorkflowError` (e.g. `STATE_LEGACY_FORMAT`, which already carries its own correct
"Re-register it with: …" remedy) passes through completely untouched, by identity — wrapping it
would double-remedy. A non-`WorkflowError` throw also passes through untouched.

issue #493 seam: if definition snapshots ever land on the run record, the snapshot-wins
resolution order belongs INSIDE this function — every run-context caller updates for free.

`@param` store Anything that can `.get()` a workflow by id.

`@param` run The run whose `workflow_id` to resolve.

`@param` opts `retryVerb` — the verb this call site's remedy should recommend retrying with
(e.g. `'re-attach'`, `'respond again'`, `'resume again'`, `'replay again'`,
`'drain again'`, or the MCP-neutral `'retry'`).

```ts
function getWorkflowForRun(store: Pick<WorkflowRegistrar, 'get'>, run: ListedRecord, opts: {
    retryVerb: string;
    verb: string;
    terminalOk?: boolean;
}): Promise<WorkflowDefinition>;
```

### judgedSnapshotOf

function · public

The run record and the reading an engine reply was judged on, for a host that judges after the
call instead of reading the run again.
FOR JUDGING,
NEVER FOR PRINTING: the record is raw (undisclosed); a sentence about it is composed through the
door's disclosed view. Carried privately: a copy of the reply (`{ ...reply }`, `structuredClone`,

### reclaimStep

function · public

Reclaims a single in-progress claim on a run. Guards (in order): store capability → terminal
run → the open-gate step → membership. With `force: true` the call is judged after the load
instead: the run ended → a step not in progress (`not_a_step`, else `not_held`) → the open-gate
step → a store that keeps no claims → the stamp (`fence_required`, `claim_changed`). Returns
idempotent success when the step is already settled. On a CAS mismatch it RE-EVALUATES the predicate (never a blind abandon-style re-remove).

```ts
function reclaimStep(store: RunStore, runId: string, stepName: string, options?: ReclaimStepOptions): Promise<ReclaimResult>;
```

### releaseDriveClaim

function · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

Gives back step `stepName`'s claim without settling the step, when that claim names `hold`'s
lease.
The run is read; the step in progress with its claim naming
`hold.id` ⇒ a `release_step` settle under the claim's own token, with `evidence` appended ⇒
`released`, or `not_released` with the store's reason; otherwise ⇒ `not_ours`, nothing written. A
read or settle that throws is thrown unchanged. It never closes the hold: the caller does, with the
record it returns.

```ts

```

function · public

A step's `prompt` rendered against the workflow's static context, with no run parameters and no
evidence, and its `StableBoundary`. The static context is its `workflow_context` files, read now.
Every placeholder a run fills is unresolved here, so it is unstable and the boundary falls at the
first of them.
With
no `prompt`, `undefined`. Async: it reads the context files; the caller gives the instant the

### withLibraryWords

function · public

The complete way renderer built from a program's partial one (`PartialWayRenderer`). The
program's function for each verb it gave
one, Realm's own words (`LIBRARY_WORDS`) for every other verb — a verb added in a later minor
release included, until the program writes its own. A member that is not a function — `undefined`
included — counts as not given. String words only, as `LIBRARY_WORDS` gives them: a renderer with

### ExtensionRegistry

class · public

The handlers, service adapters and processors a program registers by name; the engine looks a
step's handler or adapter up in it.

```ts
class ExtensionRegistry {
    register(type: 'adapter', name: string, impl: ServiceAdapter): void;
    register(type: 'processor', name: string, impl: Processor): void;
    register(type: 'handler', name: string, impl: StepHandler): void;
    setIdentity(entry: ExtensionIdentityEntry): void;
    get identity(): ExtensionIdentityEntry | undefined;
    has(type: 'adapter' | 'processor' | 'handler', name: string): boolean;
    names(type: 'adapter' | 'processor' | 'handler'): string[];
    getAdapter(name: string): ServiceAdapter | undefined;
    getProcessor(name: string): Processor | undefined;
    getHandler(name: string): StepHandler | undefined;
    getOrCreateRateLimiter(serviceName: string, config: RateLimitConfig): RateLimiter;
}
```

### JsonFileStore

class · public

The run store that keeps each run as a JSON file, `<runId>.json`, in its runs folder.

GLOBAL LOCK ORDER (issue #184): run-file lock BEFORE key lock, never the reverse.
`deleteAllForRun` is the only site that nests them (run-file lock held, key lock acquired
inside it, key lock released, then the run file is deleted and the run-file lock released).
Every other method that touches both takes them SEQUENTIALLY, never nested: `save()` releases
its run-file lock before `registerImportedKey()` acquires the key lock; `create()` only ever
takes the key lock (the run file it writes under that lock is a fresh path, not yet lockable
meaningfully — no run-file lock is held during `create()`). Violating this order (acquiring a
key lock and THEN a run-file lock while still holding the key lock) is the classic two-lock
deadlock shape and must never be introduced.

#616 PR-2c c4-i: the class no longer declares `RunStore`, and no run-store contract runs on it; PR-3
deletes it.

```ts
class JsonFileStore implements PerRunArtifactStore {
    readonly persistsClaims = true;
    readonly persistedRunRecordFields: ReadonlySet<LoadBearingRunRecordField>;
    readonly clock: Clock;
    constructor(runsDir?: string);
    get runsDirPath(): string;
    create(options: CreateRunOptions): Promise<CreateResult>;
    get(runId: string): Promise<Snapshot>;
    update(record: RunRecord): Promise<Snapshot>;
    claimStep(runId: string, stepName: string, definition: WorkflowDefinition, claimant?: Attributed): Promise<Snapshot>;
    settleStep(runId: string, delta: SettlementDelta, definition?: WorkflowDefinition): Promise<StoreSettlement>;
    stampSeal(runId: string, sealedBy: SealedBy, expectedVersion: number): Promise<StampSealResult>;
    save(record: RunRecord): Promise<void>;
    reconcileKeys(workflowId?: string, dryRun?: boolean, options?: {
        command?: string;
    }): Promise<ReconcileSummary>;
    list(workflowId?: string): Promise<Listing>;
    listWithDiagnostics(workflowId?: string): Promise<RunListing>;
    listRunIds(): Promise<ReadonlySet<string>>;
    statAllForRun(runId: string, _dirEntries?: readonly string[]): Promise<{
        bytes: number;
    }>;
    deleteAllForRun(runId: string, _dirEntries?: readonly string[], options?: {
        expectVersion?: number;
    }): Promise<ArtifactDeletionReport>;
}
```

### EngineReply

interface · public (beta: own_act): those members may change in a minor release until they settle

The reply of every engine entry: its status and data, the ways as data, and the typed receipts.
It is the envelope without the door's words (`next_actions`, `agent_action`,
`blocked_reason.suggestion`, the way clause, `gate.claim_token`), plus what can be done next
(`ways`), what cannot and why (`unavailable`), and what they were judged on (`basis`).
Ways are never stored:
a replayed request returns its first verdict with fresh ways. Each door renders it — MCP's
`renderReply`, the CLI's `CLI_COMMANDS`; the library carries it as it is.

```ts
interface EngineReply {
    command: string;
    run_id: string;
    run_version: number;
    status: RunStatus;
    data: Record<string, unknown>;
    evidence: EvidenceSnapshot[];
    warnings: string[];
    diagnostics?: LoaderWarning[];
    errors: string[];
    error_code?: ErrorCode;
    error_details?: Record<string, unknown>;
    error?: ReplyError;
    intrinsic_action?: AgentAction;
    reply_kind: ReplyKind;
    retry_after?: number;
    context_hint: string;
    run_phase?: RunPhase;
    ways: WayOn[];
    unavailable: Unavailable[];
    basis?: Basis;
    outcome?: Outcome;
    races?: RaceEntry[];
    expiry?: ExpiryReceipt;
    refusal?: Unavailable;
    names_next?: true;
    blocked_reason?: BlockedReason;
    gate?: GateInfo;
    chained_auto_steps?: Array<{
        step: string;
        run_phase: string;
        branched_via?: string;
    }>;
    adopted_own?: number;
    adopted_anonymous?: number;
    preserved_foreign?: number;
    settled_by_default?: boolean;
    defaulted_steps?: string[];
    guards?: Array<{
        step: string;
        outcome: 'pass' | 'abort' | 'resolution_error';
    }>;
    ended_by?: {
        arm: SealArm;
        step: string;
        reason?: string;
    };
    stopped_step?: string;
    own_act?: {
        command: string;
        recorded: true;
        evidence?: EvidenceSnapshot;
    };
    answer_recorded?: false;
    gate_claim?: {
        proof: GateClaimVerdict['proof'];
        cause?: 'no_claim' | 'claim_has_no_token' | 'store_keeps_no_claims' | 'answered' | 'expired';
        opened_by: Attributed | ActorAbsent;
        carried_on?: boolean;
        not_carried_on_because?: 'nothing_runnable' | 'not_settled_by_this_call' | 'proof_absent' | 'proof_mismatch' | 'proof_unverifiable' | 'no_registry' | 'extensions_differ' | 'extensions_not_comparable';
        chain_stopped?: 'budget';
        continued_by?: Attributed | ActorAbsent;
        answered_by?: {
            by: string;
```

### Outcome

interface · public

What an answer that was not recorded met: the choice recorded instead and how, or the gate
cancelled when a step ended the run. `answer` by a person, `timeout` by the question's expiry;
`engine`, with no choice, when a step ended the run (a cancelled gate chose nothing).
`at` is the winning entry's `completed_at`; `by.name` comes from
`responded_by`, always `basis: 'stated'` — realm never claims who was on the other end. `step` and
`expiry` are the question's, from the call's snapshot taken before any wait; `attempted` says
whether THIS call tried to answer. Data in PR-0; W's `renderOutcome` renders it.

#729 PR-6a (B2): `attempted_choice` is this call's own choice — present exactly when `attempted` is
true and the call gave one; `by.name` is read through core's one reader of a stated name
(`readStatedAnswerer`): no name, or a blank one, gives no `name`; a name that reader refuses gives
`name_absent: 'name_unreadable'` instead.

```ts
interface Outcome {
    choice?: string;
    attempted_choice?: string;
    by: {
        kind: 'answer';
        name?: string;
        name_absent?: 'name_unreadable';
        account?: string;
        account_absent?: 'account_unreadable';
        basis: 'stated';
    } | {
        kind: 'timeout';
    } | {
        kind: 'engine';
        cause: 'gate_cancelled_by_abort';
        step: string;
        name?: string;
        basis?: 'stated';
    };
    at?: string;
    step: string;
    expiry?: string;
    attempted: boolean;
    via?: string | {
        absent: 'settled_by_expiry' | 'recorded_without_route' | 'route_not_declared';
    };
}
```

interface · public

(`ExecuteStepOptions.stepMeta`).

Present (possibly []) when tools were declared.

`structuredOutput` (issue #236) — the caller's own `structured_output: 'strict'` attempt
disclosure for THIS attempt.

`usage` (issue #600) — what the provider said each WIRE REQUEST cost, in wire order.

The three are INDEPENDENT: any one alone must still cause `stepMeta` to be passed. Named (not
inlined twice) so `ExecuteStepOptions` and `ExecuteChainOptions` cannot drift apart.

```ts

    structuredOutput?: StructuredOutputMeta;
    usage?: UsageRecord[];
    modelText?: ModelText;
    modelAttempts?: ModelAttempt[];
}
```

type · public

What a capability refusal was judged from: the caller's own registry, or the run's marker when

type · public

(`ExecuteChainOptions.caller`).

### ClaimableErrorClass

type · public

An `error_class` word a provider or a program may claim: every word but `startup_failure`, which
only `realm agent`'s and `realm listen`'s own startup writers mint. Q1 (#592) unit c.

```ts
type ClaimableErrorClass = Exclude<DriveFailureRecord['error_class'], 'startup_failure'>;
```

### ClaimState

type · public

How alive a single in-progress claim is: `healthy`, `claim_stale` or `claim_unknown_age`. The
states:
- `healthy` — a concrete deadline that has not yet passed.
- `claim_stale` — a concrete deadline that has passed.
- `claim_unknown_age` — no claim record, or a `null` deadline (agent / finalizer-bearing /
  legacy run). Detect-only, human-judged, NEVER auto-reclaimed.

#729 CW-1b: a claim that names a lease is judged by its lease's fact instead (design record C5
§4.4): `held` ⇒ `healthy`; `not_held` ⇒ `claim_stale`; `absent` or `unknown` ⇒ `claim_unknown_age`.

```ts
type ClaimState = 'healthy' | 'claim_stale' | 'claim_unknown_age';
```

### Cond

type · public

A condition a way is offered with: a way offered with a condition is admitted only when the
condition is met (`Base.conditions`).
PR-0's one member: `enactor_has` — the step needs a handler or
an adapter, and whether this program has it is judged from its `basis`: `marker` (the run's own
`capability_blocks` record: the program that last attempted the step lacked it), `unjudged` (an
observer passed no registry — C33: a read surface never executes project code), `load_failed` (this
program's project code failed to load).

W added `client_prompt`; PR-1 adds `confirm_after_preview`, `erases_operator_ending`,
`override_claim_unknown_age` — each with its producer, never reserved here. The gate-answers default
(2026-11-14) removed `client_prompt`'s one producer, the MCP door's fallback row; the member and its
tag stay, as exported names, and nothing composes it now.

```ts
type Cond = {
    code: 'enactor_has';
    kind: 'handler' | 'adapter';
    name: string;
    basis: 'marker' | 'unjudged' | 'load_failed';
} | {
    code: 'client_prompt';
    tag: CondTag;
} | {
    code: 'claim_deadline_ahead';
    deadline: string;
} | {
    code: 'override_claim_unknown_age';
    state: 'unknown_age' | 'unreadable' | 'no_claim_record';
} | {
    code: 'lease_held';
} | {
    code: 'rerun_not_idempotent';
    basis: 'not_declared' | 'definition_absent';
};
```

### DisclosureTier

type · public

`declared` hides declared members only (question text, private terminals); `all` adds the
environment members and the patterns.

```ts
type DisclosureTier = 'declared' | 'all';
```

### DriveClaim

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

What `claimStepForDrive` answers, keyed by `kind`. The union is open: later units add kinds
(Q2-a's `over_limit`), so a caller handles an unknown `kind` as a refusal.
- `claimed`: the step's claim is this program's, under `hold`, taken at `since`. The caller holds
  the lease until it closes it.
- `held_by`: another program holds the step. `holder` and `since` are its claim's, and `lease` its
  lease's fact, when the run still shows that claim (and it names a lease).
- `not_eligible`: the step cannot run now.
- `refused`: the step was refused for another reason, by its code.
- `lease_unavailable`: the store could not make a lease, with why; no claim was taken.
- `unleased_store`: the store keeps no leases; nothing was held, read or written.

```ts
type DriveClaim = {
    readonly kind: 'claimed';
    readonly hold: LeaseHold;
    readonly since: string;
} | {
    readonly kind: 'held_by';
    readonly holder?: Attributed;
    readonly since?: string;
    readonly lease?: LeaseFact;
} | {
    readonly kind: 'not_eligible';
} | {
    readonly kind: 'refused';
    readonly code: Exclude<UnavailableCode, 'held_elsewhere' | 'not_eligible'>;
} | {
    readonly kind: 'lease_unavailable';
    readonly reason: LeaseUnavailableReason;
} | {
    readonly kind: 'unleased_store';
};
```

### DriveRelease

type · beta: may change in a minor release until it settles

What `releaseDriveClaim` answers: `released`, `not_released` or `not_ours` (`kind`).
Each comes with the snapshot it was judged on or the one the store's settle returned:
- `released`: the claim is gone and the step can run again;
- `not_released`: the store refused the release, with its own reason;
- `not_ours`: the step is not in progress, or its claim names no lease or another; nothing was
  written.

```ts
type DriveRelease = {
    readonly kind: 'released';
    readonly snapshot: Snapshot;
} | {
    readonly kind: 'not_released';
    readonly reason: SettlementRefusalReason;
    readonly snapshot: Snapshot;
} | {
    readonly kind: 'not_ours';
    readonly snapshot: Snapshot;
};
```

### EnactedVia

type · public

The call that carried out an expired question's declared `on_expiry`, as `enacted_via` names it.
It is the word the expiry's line ends with: the caller of the entry that carried it out
(`advanceRun`, `executeStep`, `executeChain`, `submitHumanResponse`, or the name the host passed:
an MCP tool, a CLI command), or `timer`, the waiting process's own timer (`realm agent`, `realm
workflow run`), which writes a line of its own.

```ts
type EnactedVia = AdvanceCaller | StepCaller | EngineStepCaller | ChainCaller | AnswerCaller | 'timer';
```

```ts
        name: string;
    };
} | {
    cause: 'another_program_holds_it';
} | {
    cause: 'already_settled';
} | {
    cause: 'engine_runs_it_when_owed';
};
```

### NotRecordedKind

type · public

The four kinds of a race in which this call's handler ran (`ran_here: true`).

```ts
type NotRecordedKind = Extract<RaceStopKind, 'held_elsewhere' | 'step_settled' | 'run_ended' | 'claim_removed'>;
```

### PartialWayRenderer

type · public

The renderer a program supplies when it words some of a reply's `ways` itself: any of
`WayRenderer`'s functions, each one optional. `withLibraryWords` completes it with
Realm's own words (`LIBRARY_WORDS`), so a verb added in a later minor release renders with
Realm's words until the program writes its own. String words only, as `LIBRARY_WORDS` gives them:
a renderer with another output type has no default and is written whole, as a `WayRenderer`.

```ts
type PartialWayRenderer<Host> = Partial<WayRenderer<string, Host>>;
```

### Party

type · public

Who can take a way on a run: the operator, the agent, or the person a question is asked of
(`WAY_PARTIES`, `ForWay.for`).

```ts
type Party = (typeof PARTIES)[number];
```

### PreClaimRefusal

type · public

The checks that refuse a step before it is claimed: its trust, its precondition, its input
schema, its capability.

```ts
type PreClaimRefusal = (typeof PRE_CLAIM_REFUSALS)[number];
```

### PresentWay

type · public

Show the open question again, as a form in the agent's own call: the MCP door's
`present_question`.
The agent cannot answer through it: the person's accept records the
answer. No `step`: a renderer reads the step from the reply it already holds.

```ts
type PresentWay = Base<'present'> & {
    run_id: string;
    gate_id: string;
};
```

### RaceStopKind

type · public

The six race kinds: another program got there first, and the loop goes on with what is left.

```ts
type RaceStopKind = Exclude<StopKind, HaltStopKind>;
```

### ReclaimOutcome

type · public

What `reclaimStep` did: moved the claim out, so the step can run again; nothing, as the step was
already settled or held no claim; or left a claim another program had just taken.

```ts
type ReclaimOutcome = 'reclaimed' | 'already_settled' | 'taken_over' | 'no_active_claim';
```

### ReclaimWay

type · public

Free a held step so it can run again: a person's act, never an agent's. Its conditions say what
holds, each discharged by `force`; `claimed_at` is the claim's stamp, present exactly when the claim
carries one, so the act applies only to the claim it was shown (#922).

```ts
type ReclaimWay = Base<'reclaim'> & {
    run_id: string;
    step: string;
    claimed_at?: string;
};
```

### RefusedCheck

type · public

The checks other than capability that refuse a step before its claim (`checkPreClaim`).

```ts
type RefusedCheck = 'trust' | 'precondition' | 'input_schema';
```

### RegisterWay

type · public

Register the run's workflow again. No judge admits it; on MCP it is the operator's, done outside
the conversation (the door renders no instruction).
`path` only
when the registry knows the file (T-21: the unreadable, invalid, legacy and newer copies carry
it): the registered COPY that cannot be used — never a file to register (correction 2, 3.2: each
door words it as a copy to repair).

`copy` (#616 PR-2c c10a-4c) says the registered copy EXISTS but cannot be used, whether or not it
has a file: a copy in a database has none, so `path` alone cannot tell it from a copy that is not
there. The doors read it; the library's own words (`LIBRARY_WORDS`) do not, because the library's
repair is the same act either way.

```ts
type RegisterWay = Base<'register'> & {
    workflow_id: string;
    run_id?: string;
    path?: string;
    copy?: 'unusable';
};
```

### ReplyKind

type · public

The kinds of reply `agentActionOf` tells apart: ok, confirm required, refusal, blocked, error.

```ts
type ReplyKind = (typeof REPLY_KINDS)[number];
```

### RespondWay

type · public

Answer the run's open question.

```ts
type RespondWay = Base<'respond'> & {
    run_id: string;
    gate_id: string;
    step: string;
    choice: Slot<string>;
    expires_at?: string;
    on_expiry?: 'settle_default' | 'abort';
    holds: readonly string[];
    presented: 'with_gate' | 'alone';
    has_message?: true;
    owner?: string;
    proof?: {
        claim_token: string;
    };
};
```

### RunStatus

type · public

The status of an engine reply: `ok`, `error`, `blocked` (the wrong step for the run's state) or
`confirm_required` (a question is open) (`EngineReply.status`).

```ts
type RunStatus = 'ok' | 'error' | 'blocked' | 'confirm_required';
```

### RunStepWay

type · public

Run one step: an agent step's answer, or an engine step's input given by the operator.

```ts
type RunStepWay = Base<'run_step'> & {
    run_id: string;
    step: string;
    brief: StepBrief;
};
```

### StepCaller

type · public

The names a call to `executeStep` can give for where it came from (`ExecuteStepOptions.caller`).

```ts
type StepCaller = (typeof ENTRY_CALLERS.executeStep)[number];
```

### StepDispatcher

type · public

The host's dispatcher for a step. issue #719 (C4): it may return the step's output as a plain
value, as well as through a promise.

```ts
type StepDispatcher = (stepName: string, input: Record<string, unknown>, run: RunRecord, signal?: AbortSignal) => Promise<Record<string, unknown>> | Record<string, unknown>;
```

### StopClassification

type · public

What `classifyStop` returns.

```ts
type StopClassification = RaceStop | HaltStop;
```

### StopKind

type · public

Why a loop stopped on a step it picked or ran: six races, after which it goes on with what is
left, and three kinds that stop it.

```ts
type StopKind = (typeof STOP_KINDS)[number];
```

### Unavailable

type · public

A way that cannot be taken now, with its code, its facts and the remedies that lead on.

```ts
type Unavailable = {
    [C in UnavailableCode]: {
        verb: WayVerb;
        step?: string;
        code: C;
        facts: FactsOf<C>;
        clears_at?: string;
        remedy: readonly WayOn[];
        no_remedy?: NoRemedy;
    };
}[UnavailableCode];
```

### UnavailableCode

type · public

The codes that say why a way cannot be taken now, one per reason (`Unavailable.code`).

```ts
type UnavailableCode = keyof typeof UNAVAILABLE_CODES;
```

### WayOf

type · public

The way of one verb.

```ts
type WayOf<V extends WayVerb> = Extract<WayOn, {
    verb: V;
}>;
```

### WayOn

type · public

One act a party can take on a run, told apart by its `verb`.

```ts
type WayOn = RespondWay | RunStepWay | AdvanceWay | InspectWay | AbandonWay | RegisterWay | PresentWay | ReclaimWay;
```

### WayRenderer

type · public

A door's renderer table, keyed by verb: it must cover every `WayVerb`, so a new verb is a
compile-time decision in every table. An entry
takes ONE way, its basis stamp and the host's static settings — never a record, view, definition,
registry, clock or snapshot (the renderer law; the import census and the `Date` ban witness it).
A door that never renders a verb returns `null`, with its reason in a comment.

```ts
type WayRenderer<Out, Host> = {
    readonly [V in WayVerb]: (way: WayOf<V>, basis: Basis | undefined, host: Host) => Out | null;
};
```

### WayVerb

type · public

The acts a way names: answer a question, run a step, have the engine carry out what it owes, read
the run, end it, register its workflow again, or send a question's form to the person
(`Base.verb`).

```ts
type WayVerb = (typeof WAY_VERBS)[number];
```

## Constants

### ACTOR_ABSENT_CAUSES

const · public

Why a name is absent. All derived AT READ, never stored. #558 PR-V adds its own members to this
const; no second absence type exists.

```ts
const ACTOR_ABSENT_CAUSES: readonly [
    "holder_not_recorded",
    "pre_lease_claim",
    "no_claim",
    "store_keeps_no_claims",
    "driver_not_recorded",
    "name_unreadable",
    "not_stated",
    "settled_by_expiry"
];
```

### CAPABILITY_BASES

const · public

What a capability refusal was judged from: the caller's own registry, or the run's marker when
the caller passed no registry. `registry`: the caller's own registry lacks the handler or
adapter; `marker`: the caller passed no registry, so the run's own `capability_blocks` marker
(what the runner that last attempted the step lacked) is the fact.

```ts
const CAPABILITY_BASES: readonly [
    "registry",
    "marker"
];
```

### ENTRY_CALLERS

const · public

The words the engine's entries name themselves by, one closed list per entry.
The word is the call the expiry line names (`this <caller> call first carried out …
(enacted_via: <caller>).`) when that call carries out an expired question's declared
`on_expiry`, and, for `advanceRun`, the reply's `command` unless `command` is given. The first
word of each list is the default: the library function itself, a program's own call. The others
are the hosts that call it and pass their own name — the MCP tools (`advance_run`, `start_run`,
`execute_step`, `submit_human_response`) and the CLI commands (`advance` is `realm run advance`,
`agent` is `realm agent`, `run` is `realm workflow run`, `respond` is `realm run respond`). No
word names a call that is not made (round 20's finding 5: `executeEngineStep` admits its own call).
Never a free string: `command` is `advanceRun`'s free label.

```ts
const ENTRY_CALLERS: {
    readonly advanceRun: readonly [
        "advanceRun",
        "advance_run",
        "advance",
        "start_run",
        "agent",
        "submit_human_response",
        "submitHumanResponse"
    ];
    readonly executeStep: readonly [
        "executeStep",
        "agent"
    ];
    readonly executeEngineStep: readonly [
        "executeEngineStep",
        "agent"
    ];
    readonly executeChain: readonly [
        "executeChain",
        "execute_step",
        "agent",
        "run"
    ];
    readonly submitHumanResponse: readonly [
        "submitHumanResponse",
        "submit_human_response",
        "respond",
        "run",
        "agent"
    ];
};
```

### LIBRARY_WORDS

const · public

The library door's words for each way: the library function an embedder calls to take it, never a
CLI command or an MCP tool.
Applied by embedders to a reply's
`ways`; never imported by core's composers (the witness reads that). A way's words come from the
way alone (the renderer law).

```ts
const LIBRARY_WORDS: WayRenderer<string, LibraryHost>;
```

const · public

Who can take a way: the operator, the agent, or the person a question is asked of.

```ts
const PARTIES: readonly [
    "operator",
    "agent",
    "asked_person"
];
```

### PRE_CLAIM_REFUSALS

const · public

The checks that refuse a step before it is claimed, in the order `executeStep` runs them.

```ts
const PRE_CLAIM_REFUSALS: readonly [
    "trust",
    "precondition",
    "input_schema",
    "capability"
];
```

### REPLY_KINDS

const · public

The kinds of reply `agentActionOf` tells apart.

```ts
const REPLY_KINDS: readonly [
    "ok",
    "confirm_required",
    "refusal",
    "blocked",
    "error"
];
```

### RUN_STATUSES

const · public

Every status a reply's `status` can hold, in the type's order.
Compile-checked both ways: a word added to the type and not to the list fails the build,
and so does a word in the list the type does not have (Q1, #592, unit d1b).

```ts
const RUN_STATUSES: readonly [
    "ok",
    "error",
    "blocked",
    "confirm_required"
];
```

### STOP_KINDS

const · public

The kinds of stop a loop meets on a step it picked or ran (`StopKind`).
The
first six are races — another program got there first, and the loop goes on with what is left:
`held_elsewhere` (another program holds the step, or ran it before this call claimed it),
`step_settled` (another program settled the step this call ran), `run_ended`, `claim_removed` (the
claim this call held was removed and nobody settled the step: it is owed again), `question_open`,
`not_eligible` (the claim's own re-check refused it, and the record shows nothing more). The last
three stop the loop: `capability_missing` (this program lacks the step's handler or adapter), and
the error kinds `failed` (the record lists the step the reply is about as failed) and `refused`.

```ts
const STOP_KINDS: readonly [
    "held_elsewhere",
    "step_settled",
    "run_ended",
    "claim_removed",
    "question_open",
    "not_eligible",
    "capability_missing",
    "failed",
    "refused"
];
```

```ts
    "run_step",
    "advance",
```
